summary: Bounded attainment forces J=0; actual invariant variations identify the equation at a strictly convex invariant attained weight.
detailedSummary: For every fast sequence under bounded attainment, R=q, nu=MA(q), J=0 and u=q almost everywhere for prescribed and bounded-product measures. An attained smooth invariant positive-definite coordinate Hessian implies mu=MA(q); zero full dual characterizes theta^2 among all eligible measures. General attainment/representation/existence remains open.
text:
New bounded-attainment and invariant-variation deductions use only earlier own note n1 at its declared analytic-foundation boundary. General attainment is not proved.

If an actual normalized q in C attains D(mu)=B, EVERY fast maximizing sequence satisfies I(a_n,q)<=4epsilon_n. Energy and weak-test moduli give e=E(q), nu=MA(q); full-point atoms give ell=q at every full point. The all-affinoid Shilov formula then gives R=q: the boundary maximum is at least the local q value, while continuity and affinoid neighborhoods inside arbitrarily small ordinary neighborhoods give the reverse inequality after infimizing. Consequently u<=q and s=intu mu<=intq mu=E(q)-B=r. Earlier s>=r forces J=0 and u=q mu-almost everywhere. Fixed bounded-MA L1 limits of a_n are both q, by the I modulus, and u, by the fast tails; hence they agree. Mixed measures are dominated by twice a midpoint MA measure. Global all-point C/G recognition of u, and generally mu=MA(q), do not follow from this argument.

An attained invariant slice DOES identify the equation. Suppose q(x)=qbar(tau(x)) is smooth periodic with I_2+Hess(qbar) positive definite everywhere, and q attains the full dual for an eligible arbitrary-support mu. Put lambda=MA(q). Coordinate dimension and identity calibration give lambda supported on the Gauss section with raw density2det(I_2+Hess(qbar))dr_1dr_2. For every smooth periodic h, compactness supplies a uniform positive Hessian bound for q and a finite Hessian bound for h. Thus q+t h(tau) is in the actual smooth CLD class for both signs of sufficiently small t. First variation at the maximum gives int h(tau)(lambda-mu)=0. Smooth periodic convolution proves density in continuous torus tests, so tau_*lambda=tau_*mu.

For every a in C, a(x)<=a(Gauss(tau(x))). Projection equality and skeletal support of lambda give int a mu<=int a lambda. Conversely the ACTUAL segment (1-t)q+ta has nonpositive right derivative at the maximum: int(a-q)(lambda-mu)<=0. Projection equality gives intq(lambda-mu)=0, so the opposite inequality holds. Equality on C and density of its real span give equality of the actual finite Radon measures. This uses no positivity margin for arbitrary smooth perturbations.

In particular, on the ENTIRE eligible arbitrary-support class, D(mu)=0 iff mu=theta^2. If D(mu)=0, q=0 attains the dual and has coordinate Hessian I_2, so the preceding proof applies. Conversely tangent concavity at0 gives D(theta^2)=0. Skeletal support is forced as a conclusion on this slice, not imposed on the input. This supplies no every-measure attainment or existence theorem.

Complete proofs are in new-residual-proofs.tex and standalone.tex. Original analytic representation, general J/K vanishing, general variations, nonalgebraization/coherent-descent certification and full prescribed-measure existence/uniqueness remain open. No atom is claimed solved.
